item.title: Games Workshop has released a new trailer for Astartes II, the most anticipated Warhammer 40,000 animation ever.
item.description:
Games Workshop has released a new trailer for Astartes II, the most anticipated Warhammer 40,000 animation ever.
For the uninitiated, the original Astartes was created by superfan Syama Pedersen, who was subsequently brought into the fold to make the official sequel. Astartes is widely accepted as the greatest Warhammer 40,000 animation ever made, official or unofficial, with only Amazon’s excellent Space Marine 2 animation for the Secret Level anthology series competing with it in quality terms. Indeed, Astartes was so good that it inspired Saber Interactive’s hugely successful Space Marine 2 in terms of the look and feel of the Space Marines themselves.
During Games Workshop’s ‘Big Autumn Preview’ event, fans were treated to a new look at Astartes II, which confirms the appearance of Deathwatch and Terminators. As the company notes in a post on Warhammer Community, fans of Space Hulk will no doubt find a lot familiar here.
ASTARTES 2 teaserComing DecemberWe get to follow a Deathwatch unit investigating a Space Hulk! pic.twitter.com/DgveN5yz6K
Indeed, the Space Hulk vibes come through loud and clear. We see Space Marines stomp about a dark, shadowy interior which you just know will house horrible, nightmarish things in the shadows. But the first-person shot of a corridor lit only by spotlights is the clearest sign that the much-loved tabletop game, Space Hulk, was an influence.
Also in the post, Games Workshop confirmed that Astartes II will be “significantly longer” than its predecessor, which is music to fan ears. Understandably as a single-person fan project, Astartes is on the short side.
“We knew already that this was likely to feature Deathwatch and Terminators, from the unsubtle hints dropped at the end of the LAST trailer, and now we see them, they look like they mean business,” Games Workshop said. “The imposing line of storm bolter barrels and the crackle of a power fist, combined with the ominous surroundings, are certainly giving off some strong Space Hulk vibes.
“Somehow even more intimidating than the blank visage of the Terminator helms is that unhelmeted Space Marine veteran, who could certainly be described as ‘grizzled.’ And we think we clocked at least three different characters and Chapters of Space Marines in that trailer.”
In November last year, Games Workshop revealed animation work on a monitor screen via the promo video, below, that showed a squad of Terminators appearing to protect an unnamed human soldier. This was the Inquisition-led Deathwatch Terminator squad from the debut Astartes 2 teaser in incomplete form, but we know from their pauldron chapter symbols that they’re the same as before (Retributors, Mortifactors, Scythes of The Emperor, Sons of Medusa, and Angels Vermilion).
Last year’s teaser suggested an animation on a scale and quality never-before-seen from Warhammer 40,000, with melee combat, shooting, vehicle combat, and even spaceship battles all showcased. It showed a number of Space Marine chapters in battle across varied environments, and multiple enemy races, including Tyranids, Orks, and Tau.
But it turned out that nothing in the teaser is actually in the Astartes 2 animation itself. According to a post on the Warhammer Community website: “This teaser trailer is not actually clips from the new animation, instead showing a compilation of shots that represent the former lives of the characters that will appear in the show. There’s a pretty unsubtle hint at the end as to the nature of the final story... We’ll leave you to speculate and start putting the pieces together yourselves.”
Astartes II is due out this December on Warhammer+, Games Workshop’s streaming service.
Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

item.title: Paramount's World War Z sequel is moving forward, with Brad Pitt confirmed to return and Conclave's Edward Berger attached to direct.
item.description:
Paramount's World War Z sequel is moving forward, with Brad Pitt confirmed to return and Conclave's Edward Berger attached to direct.
It's two major updates for the post-apocalyptic zombie follow-up that arrived via Deadline. The site said that deals are closed, confirming that World War Z 2 – or whatever it ends up being called – has already nailed down two of the biggest question marks following its announcement in April of this year.
Deadline also reported that Plan B Entertainment's Pitt, Dede Gardner, and Jeremy Kleiner will produce, with Berger also in the mix as an executive producer. Another update is that Dennis Kelly, the creator of TV series Utopia and writer behind 2021's Together, will pen the World War Z sequel's script. It otherwise still seems to be in the early days for the project, as no additional details regarding its plot, release date, or casting have been revealed.
The World War Z IP is being reheated 13 years after the original film successfully introduced audiences to a live-action adaptation of Max Brooks' 2000s novel. Pitt starred in the first film and has expressed interest in returning to the franchise for some time, but getting it off the ground and back into the zombie horde has proven to be quite the challenge for the last decade. As his roles in movies like Once Upon a Time in... Hollywood and F1 have come and gone, so too have hopes for the sequel.
Issues with confirming a director aside, fans started to expect that a follow-up would never come to be when Paramount put it on the back burner in 2019. The Social Network and Zodiac director David Fincher was even said to be involved at one point, but despite him comparing his ideas for a take to The Last of Us, that version of World War Z never materialized. Berger has now taken the reins.
Berger turned heads when Conclave premiered in 2024, but he's got more than just the Ralph Fiennes movie under his belt. He also directed 2022's critically acclaimed war film All Quiet on the Western Front, as well as 2014's Jack. He's also said to be involved with Matt Damon's new Jason Bourne movie, though that particular project's status is somewhat of a mystery.
The specifics surrounding Pitt's return to World War Z are unclear. Although the events of the first film could put his character, Gerry Lane, front and center once again, story information has not been revealed. When World War Z 2 does come out, it will mark a reunion for Pitt and Berger, who recently worked together on The Riders. Deadline reported that the former pitched the idea of more World War Z to the latter while working on the project, with the pair ready to get to get back to work by the time production came to an end.
The World War Z sequel has no release date, but at the speed things are moving at now, it may not be too long before we hear more. While we wait, you can read IGN's 7.6/10 review for the original movie, which earned $540 million at the box office (via Box Office Mojo). You can also see why the developers behind the World War Z video game might feel at least partially responsible for the existence of a sequel.
Photo by Jason Kempin/Getty Images.

item.title: A new species of small, spotted wild cat -- leopardus tilcayo or the tilcayo tiger cat -- was discovered in Bolivia where it been mistaken by the man who took it in as a kitten.
item.description:
A new breed of cat has been discovered for the first time in 100 years.
Citing the journal Current Biology, NBC News reports that a new wild cat species dubbed leopardus tilcayo (or the tilcayo tiger cat) was discovered in the Bolivian Yungas. The exact size of this particular cat population in the wild remains unclear.
The tilcayo tiger cat is smaller than the average house cat, has rounded ears, a slender build, and is spotted.
A new species of cat has been identified for the first time in a century—and experts think that there may be even more to discover around the world: https://t.co/woOXXxJOXB pic.twitter.com/OX12m8wV3V
Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz, the co-author of Current Biology’s study, came upon the cat while volunteering for a wildlife rehabilitation center in Bolivia and thought it looked just different enough to warrant further investigation.
“The cat had been brought in by a man living in a community in the forest near La Paz who had mistaken the cat for a domestic kitten, according to details recorded by the sanctuary,” NBC reports. “He had fed the animal noodles, rice and eggs, only to realize it was wild and that he could not take care of it. So he brought it to the sanctuary.”
It was originally believed to have been a known species of wild cat, but Nogales-Ascarrunz conducted genetic testing that ultimately determined this was its own distinct cat species.
While leopardus tilcayo may be a new discovery for researchers, its existence is old news to local peoples in Bolivia who have been aware of its existence for years.
Scientists have discovered a new species of cat for the first time in over a century.Smaller than an average housecat and covered in leopard-like spots, the cat species — proposed name Leopardus tilcayo — lives in Bolivia’s Yungas forest ecoregion. Very little is known about… pic.twitter.com/2dFDkgDzKi
“This cat, they call it tilcayo. And when you ask, ‘Does it have some meaning in Quechua or Almyra and other Indigenous languages?’ they say, ‘No, my grandpa told me that’s the tilcayo,’” Nogales-Ascarrunz said. “This is a traditional knowledge that they have in the community. We want to preserve that knowledge and we didn’t want to give it another name.”
Nogales-Ascarrunz’s biggest concern about the little cat is preserving the species’ existence. The five tiger cat species native to Central and South America exist in habitats where conservation is already imperiled by development and the expansion of agriculture.

item.title: Reacher star Alan Ritchson is reportedly in talks to star in PlayStation's upcoming Helldivers movie.
item.description:
Reacher star Alan Ritchson is reportedly in talks to star in PlayStation's upcoming Helldivers movie.
As reported by Deadline, the feature film adaptation of Arrowhead Game Studios' brutal multiplayer hit is zeroing in on a new lead after Aquaman actor Jason Momoa exited the project earlier this year. Ritchson is only said to be in talks for the unnamed Helldivers role so far, but Sony and director Justin Lin will want to move fast if they still want to hit their video game-to-movie adaptation's November 2027 drop date.
Ritchson has emerged as one of the more memorable action faces in the last decade. Although he's best known as the face of Prime Video's Reacher series, he's also shown up in Supergirl, Titans, and Fast X. Most recently, viewers may recognize him from his work in Netflix's War Machine or in this month's Owen Wilson movie, Runner.
Plot details for the Helldivers movie remain tightly under wraps as the crew tries to pin Ritchson behind the scenes. Sony announced plans to bring the battle for Super Earth to the big screen back in January 2025, and although things seemed to be progressing smoothly enough since, a few snags have kept it from landing.
For example, Lin, the director behind some The Fast and the Furious movies, boarded Helldivers in December of last year. Momoa then followed as Sony nailed down a release date in February of this year.
As much sense as it would make to see Momoa buzzing through Terminids and Automatons in the name of liberty, the DC and Game of Thrones star was said to have bailed on Helldivers in June. Why he departed the movie still remains unclear, though fans probably aren't too beaten up over the idea now that Ritchson could be the one to suit up.
Helldivers is still careening toward its November 10, 2027, theatrical release date. While Sony and Ritchson hammer out the details, you can read about how Arrowhead is involved in the production and what its CEO had to say to the director.
Photo by Kierra Thorn/Getty Images.

item.title: IGN can exclusively reveal that the first-ever public screening of Hirayasumi Anime will take place during a one-night event on October 7 at New York City's Japan Society, giving fans an early look at Episode 1 before the series officially debuts in 2027.
item.description:
IGN can exclusively reveal that the first-ever public screening of Hirayasumi Anime will take place during a one-night event on October 7 at New York City's Japan Society, giving fans an early look at Episode 1 before the series officially debuts in 2027.
The event will kick off at 7pm ET, and the night will also feature a panel where composer Kaori Sawada, producer Junichi Katsutani, and VIZ Media's Godswill Ugwa will discuss what it was like bringing the acclaimed manga to the screen.
If you'd like to attend, you can grab tickets right here!
For those unfamiliar, Hirayasumi has been a huge global success and has been serialized in Weekly Big Comic Spirits since 2021. The manga has more than 1.7 million copies in circulation worldwide across ten volumes, and it was the recipient of the 71st Shogakukan Manga Award alongside being named Best Serial Comic at Lucca Comics & Games 2024.
"At 29 years old, carefree Hiroto Ikuta doesn’t have a girlfriend, a full-time job, or a plan for the future—and he couldn’t be happier," Hirayasumi's official description reads. "Hiroto’s breezy attitude isn’t easy for everyone to understand, though. In a world filled with anxiety, confusion, and grief, Hiroto and the people around him are all just doing their best to figure out this thing called life."
Once again, fans interested in attending the event can grab their tickets right here, and you can also watch the anime's official teaser trailer below.
Adam Bankhurst is a writer for IGN. You can follow him on X/Twitter @AdamBankhurst, Instagram, and TikTok, and listen to his show, Talking Disney Magic.

item.title: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil is out today, and it's already the highest-rated video game movie of all time on Rotten Tomatoes.
item.description:
Zach Cregger's Resident Evil is out today, and it's already the highest-rated video game movie of all time on Rotten Tomatoes.
The scores are in, and at least as far as the review-aggregating website is concerned, the latest shot at a live-action adaptation of Capcom's beloved survival horror series has received the best reaction of any game movie to date. Resident Evil, which was directed by Weapons' Cregger and stars Austin Abrams, boasts a 96% critics' rating at the time of this story's publication, placing it multiple percentage points above a shortlist of other well-received adaptations, including Sonic the Hedgehog 3 (86%), Werewolves Within (86%), and The Angry Birds Movie 2 (72%).
Video games have a long history of what has been deemed by many to be mediocre releases. Although many of those — including 2001's Tomb Raider and 1993's Super Mario Bros. — arrived early in the industry's life, recent years have had their fill of poorly received projects, too. Both Five Nights at Freddy's movies, despite pulling in plenty of love from audiences, failed to impress critics, and 2024's Borderlands fell just 11 places short of being the worst-rated video game movie of all time. What we're saying is that it's not exactly been stiff competition for Resident Evil, but don't let that dampen its impact.
Despite Cregger making a splash with his last two horror movies, the director has faced an uphill battle with his latest flick. Fans expecting the movie to stick closer to the lore were let down to see Abrams playing an original character in a live-action Raccoon City that looked a bit different than they may have been hoping for. Instead of Leon S. Kennedy, Nemesis, or any other familiar elements, the live-action Resident Evil instead opted to focus on new character Bryan in a story inspired by the feeling of playing the games rather than their stories.
"I did not really appreciate the sentiment that, ‘We’ve been waiting forever for Leon’s story.’ And I appreciate that, and I’m sorry that’s not the story I’m bringing," Cregger said during a recent conversation with IGN. "I get it, I understand the frustration. I understand it so well because I haven’t seen the earlier [Resident Evil] movies, because they don't look like the Resident Evil that I love, so how could I be frustrated with fans who have that same attitude?"
It's been controversial, to say the least, but despite the online backlash that's seeped into Cregger's world, the critics aren't the only ones finding something to love about Resident Evil. After more than 500 verified ratings, Rotten Tomatoes has recorded a staggering 91% score from audiences. Whatever hangups you may have thought audiences would have going in, it seems the film has proven too good for most to deny.
"My only hope is that they’ll see the movie regardless of their skepticism or their disappointment that I’m not telling some of the stories that the games tell so well, and they will feel seen when they do watch the movie, and they will recognize all of the love for the games that are in this movie, because it is there," Cregger added during his talk with IGN. "This is not me just telling a story and slapping Resident Evil on it so I can get a budget. This is me telling a Resident Evil story."
Resident Evil is still just getting its feet wet when it comes to its reception, so only time will tell if it will continue to be seen in a positive light in the weeks, months, and years ahead. It's undeniably a strong start, though, with the project also expected to clear the franchise's box office record.
IGN gave it a solid rating, too, awarding it an 8/10 review. We said, "With a laser focus on putting its hero through the worst night of his life, Resident Evil is a simple and exciting survival horror story that benefits greatly from director Zach Cregger’s sensibilities."
Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

item.title: Toys 'R' Us, the once-ubiquitous toy store/mecca for 1980's kids, is set to open 120 new standalone stores this holiday season, the company announced. The expansion is in partnership with the Go! Retail Group, who first partnered with Toys 'R' Us owner WHP Global three years ago to begin the toy store back from the dead and back into retail life. There are currently 40 standalone stores nationwide as well as other locations inside select Macy's locations nationwide.
item.description:
Toys 'R' Us, the once-ubiquitous toy store/mecca for 1980s kids, is set to open 120 new standalone stores this holiday season, the company announced. The expansion is in partnership with the Go! Retail Group, who first partnered with Toys 'R' Us owner WHP Global three years ago to begin the toy store back from the dead and back into retail life. There are currently 40 standalone stores nationwide as well as other locations inside select Macy's locations nationwide.
"This is a major moment for Toys 'R' Us as we significantly expand our presence across the United States," said WHP Global Executive Vice President Jamie Uitdenhowen. "Together with our incredible partners, we are growing Toys' R' Us in unique ways to meet customers wherever they are, whether that's at a standalone store in their hometown, inside Macy's, at the airport or at a Navy Exchange."
"This holiday season represents an extraordinary expansion for Toys 'R' Us in the US, and we couldn't be more excited to bring the magic of Toys'R'Us to so many communities across the country," said Gideon Schlessinger, CEO of Go! Retail Group. "There's something special about walking into a Toys'R'Us store, especially during the holidays — the excitement of discovering the hottest toys, seeing favorite brands and characters come to life, and finding that perfect gift."
This 40-something writer has fond memories wandering the seemingly endless aisles of toys in the store as a kid – in particularly the video game aisle, which had the game box art on the walls and tickets below each one, which you'd take to a special counter if you wanted to buy the game and they'd get the real thing from a lockup area in the back for you. But the Toys 'R' Us revival will attempt to modernize the chain as well.
"Select locations will introduce new experiences at the intersection of play, entertainment and content creation, including Creator Studios, dedicated spaces where influencers, creators and toy brands can create content, unveil new products and host toy reveals, launches and special events," the company said. "Select stores will also feature candy shops and cafés, giving customers even more reasons to explore, discover and spend time at Toys 'R' Us."
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

item.title: After putting up the Steam Frame for reservation on Monday, Valve has finally sent out its emails letting people know if they're on the reservation list or on the waitlist for the new VR headset. And, predictably, scalpers are already listing Steam Frame reservations on eBay.
item.description:
After putting up the Steam Frame for reservation on Monday, Valve has finally sent out its emails letting people know if they're on the reservation list or on the waitlist for the new VR headset. And, predictably, scalpers are already listing Steam Frame reservations on eBay.
While Valve lists the 256GB Steam Frame kit for $1,059, the eBay listings start at $1,700 for the lower storage tier. If you want to get the 1TB model, that's being listed at around $2,000 by scalpers, despite Valve's $1,299 asking price.
What's especially egregious about these listings is that the Steam Frame is already expensive for what it is, due to the ongoing RAM crisis. While I'd have some wiggle room for a VR headset with Valve's open platform and incredible wireless PCVR, I'm not sure I'd spend that much money on something without OLED optics.
Unfortunately, it looks like at least some of these listings have already sold.
Luckily, the community is fighting back. Folks on the /r/steam subreddit are mobilizing to report these listings, and it seems like eBay is taking action. After sharing instructions on how to report these listings, user /u/obscenemexican added: "Update: I'm now getting flooded with emails from eBay that the reported content has been removed, huzzah! Many down, many more to go, keep it up guys!"
Meanwhile, other users in the thread have found some of the scalpers' Steam usernames in the eBay listings and have reported them to Valve. User /u/noonyIRL said: "If you want to hurt these scum more, contact them and ask for the Steam ID tied to the reservation to check their VAC/Ban status to ensure its legitimate. If they provide it, report them to Valve, if they refuse, report to eBay for failing to provide suitable evidence. Either way, this hits their account, not just their listing."
Valve did try to mitigate the risks of scalpers when it released both the Steam Machine and the Steam Frame, implementing a random lottery system tied to its preorders. When the Frame was announced on Monday, Valve opened up a sign-up system, where anyone with a Steam Account could select which version of the headset they were interested in. Then, Valve randomized the entries and split them into a bucket of reservations and a waitlist.
I'm sure that did mitigate how many scalpers would otherwise be able to get the system if it was available on a first-come, first-serve basis, but it clearly did not stop scalpers from trying to profit off of the system's scarcity. Hopefully, either eBay, Valve or both get this situation under control, so that more people are able to get the Frame at a somewhat reasonable cost.
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

item.title: Former PlayStation executives Shuhei Yoshida and Adam Boyes have recreated their iconic game-sharing instructional video as Sony helps the industry barrel toward a discless future.
item.description:
Former PlayStation executives Shuhei Yoshida and Adam Boyes have recreated their iconic game-sharing instructional video as Sony helps the industry barrel toward a discless future.
Even if you weren't playing too many games in 2013, there's a good chance you remember the "Official PlayStation Used Game Instructional Video." It was a viral 20-second how-to that saw then-Sony figureheads Boyes and Yoshida deliver a tongue-in-cheek guide for sharing physical games on PS4, racking up 21.3 million YouTube views in the 13 years since its premiere.
At the time, Sony took a clear and successful jab at Microsoft and its rocky Xbox One launch plans. Fast forward 13 years, and Sony's plan to kill physical discs will have game sharing on PlayStation looking quite different from 2028. With the end of physical discs looming, Boyes and Yoshida reunited to recreate the legendary moment at Tokyo Game Show, and unfortunately, there were no physical games to be found.
Met with a best friend :D @amboyes @PlayStation_jp #TGS2026 pic.twitter.com/2ZjsrLMNaP
"Met with a best friend," Yoshida said with an open-smile emoticon.
The two snapped a few photos together as part of Tokyo Game Show, calling back to the moment that has lived rent-free in gamers' heads for years. It was clearly a fun nod to PlayStation's past, but the future is looking grim, and fans have mixed feelings.
"This picture of Shuhei Yoshida and Adam Boyes from Tokyo Game Show is making the rounds," physical game X/Twitter account @DoesItPlay1 said. "Seemingly mocking current anti-consumer PlayStation for killing the philosophy behind their once famous pro-consumer mockery of Xbox regarding physical game sharing."
"This is how you share games with your friends in 2028," another fan added, referencing the lack of games in their hands.
How it started / How it ended pic.twitter.com/pXBz5lUbQQ
I know what you did there. pic.twitter.com/d6AztR0uIC
2013 vs 2026 🥲13 ans plus tard, Shuhei Yoshida recrée sur son compte Twitter sa photo iconique de l’E3 2013… sauf que cette fois, lui et son collègue ne s’échangent que du vent !#TokyoGameShow #PlayStation pic.twitter.com/fkJEq5yu2L
Sony announced in July of this year that it would cease physical disc production for new video games starting in January 2028. It's a move that has landed the PlayStation company in hot water for months, and despite recently soft sales for game discs, the topic isn't something fans plan to let go anytime soon.
But in July, Sony insisted its decision wasn't having any impact on its business, and it didn't predict any negative impact in the future, either. When Sony announced the news it said it was simply following consumer trends. “In response to shifting trends in consumer preference, new games will be released on PlayStation Store and at retailers in digital formats only,” Sid Shuman, Senior Director, Sony Interactive Entertainment Content Communications, said in a post on PlayStation Blog.
There are of course instances of companies reversing controversial decisions amid a backlash, but, as analysts have told IGN, it remains unlikely that Sony will U-turn on this. For Sony, going all-digital for new game releases will earn it more money from every sale at a time when console sales are expected to plummet due to their rising cost.
For a first-party PlayStation game such as Marvel's wolverine, Sony will only keep around 65% of the money from a physical copy, with around 30% going to the retailer and roughly another 5% on manufacturing costs. Meanwhile, for a physical copy of a third-party game such as the Activision-published Call of Duty, Sony will get a licensing fee, likely around 15%.
As Microsoft introduces a new feature that will allow Xbox players to digitize their physical games, it's hard not to look at the irony of where game sharing is at in 2026. While we wait to see how it all shakes out, you can read why one IGN writer called Sony's decision both concerning and offensive.
Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

item.title: Sony has yet to announce an official sales figure for Marvel’s Wolverine, but one analyst has said early data suggests it's sold 1.9 million copies since going on sale on September 15, generating around $130 million in revenue.
item.description:
Sony has yet to announce an official sales figure for Marvel’s Wolverine, but one analyst has said early data suggests it's sold 1.9 million copies since going on sale on September 15, generating around $130 million in revenue.
Rhys Elliott, head of market analysis at Alinea Analytics, took to social media to say an estimated 22.9% of that revenue came from the sale of physical copies of the game — remember, Sony plans to cease production of PlayStation discs from 2028.
Through all this, it’s important to note that Sony has yet to make any official sales announcement for Marvel’s Wolverine. It has made sales announcements for PlayStation Studios games in the past. For example, Sucker Punch’s Ghost of Yotei went on sale on October 2, 2025 and sold 3.3 million units as of November 2 (at the 32 day mark), according to Sony’s official figures.
Back in October 23, Sony announced that Insomniac's PlayStation 5 exclusive Spider-Man 2 sold more than 2.5 million copies in 24 hours, which meant the open-world superhero game overtook Santa Monica Studio’s God of War Ragnarok at the top of the PlayStation day-one launch sales chart. At the time, it was the fastest-selling PlayStation Studios game in history (Helldivers 2 now holds top spot).
Assuming Alinea Analytics is in the right ballpark, Marvel’s Wolverine is tracking behind Spider-Man 2. But it has already passed the lifetime PS5 copies sold and revenues of Hideo Kojima’s Death Stranding 2, which hit the headlines when Sony ditched Kojima’s Physint. Indeed, according to Elliot, Marvel’s Wolverine is after just a few days on sale the top-performing new PlayStation Studios game released on PS5 so far this year, ahead of MLB The Show, Bungie’s Marathon, Housemarque’s Saros, and fighting game Marvel Tōkon.
The big question is how well Wolverine continues to sell. Wolverine is currently sitting on a 77 Metascore, with IGN’s Marvel’s Wolverine review returning a 6/10. We said: “Marvel's Wolverine's slick and satisfying combat wears thin well before its conclusion, so much so that even its strong character work can't quite save it from being anything more than okay.”
“So yes, Wolverine has sold well, but its commercial long tail is limited by its mixed media and streamer reception,” Elliott said. “Unlike Spider-Man, which reviewed insanely well and has stayed evergreen for years, this one’s tail will be shorter and lumpier, but still there.”
Expect a bump when the MCU kicks into gear this December with the release of Avengers: Doomsday, which features the X-Men (but does it feature Hugh Jackman’s Wolverine?). Wolverine might also benefit from the expanded PS5 install base that will inevitably kick in with the release of GTA 6 in November. And Wolverine is sure to prove a popular choice under the Christmas tree.
“Wolverine will keep selling, just not at Spider-Man heights,” Elliott added. “Spidey’s been evergreen. Wolverine will be more ever-yellow.”
Earlier this week, Insomniac said it was planning to “further refine the player experience” based on feedback. One aspect Insomniac may be looking at is Wolverine’s infamous “fart gas,” which has become the butt of online jokes in recent weeks. Some have called for Insomniac to add the ability to disable Logan’s scent trail entirely from the game amid complaints about handholding.
Meanwhile, Marvel's Wolverine players are testing its motorcycle sequence to see if Logan can die if you don't touch the controller. Another player managed to take Logan out of bounds, revealing new areas of the game.
We’ve got 17 Essential Tips and Tricks to help you get started in Marvel’s Wolverine, plus our recommendations for the 10 Best Adaptations, and a guide on How to Farm XP Quickly. item.title: Ahead of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4’s release, Activision has spoken about the “multi-billion-dollar market” behind video game cheats.
item.description:
Ahead of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4’s release, Activision has spoken about the “multi-billion-dollar market” behind video game cheats.
Cheating is a fact of life in pretty much all online games, but Call of Duty has a reputation for it, exacerbated by the free-to-download battle royale, Warzone. Activision, like other video game companies, faces an uphill battle against cheaters and those who make and profit from them, and generative AI has made that battle even more complex.
Now, to hammer home the point about how big a deal video game cheating is, Activision's Team Ricochet has posted a blog that breaks down the business behind it.
“Cheat sellers have built a sprawling, multi-billion-dollar marketplace of resellers, subscription services, cheat reskins, illicit accounts, spoofing tools, and organized distribution networks,” Activision said, pointing to recent analysis that suggests cheat subscriptions across just 15 games generates roughly $3.5 billion annually. Activision estimates that when you include adjacent industries such as account sales, boosting, spoofing, and other services, the broader cheating economy generates about $8.5 billion each year.
You might have seen Activision post bodycam footage of a Call of Duty cheat maker being served a cease and desist order — that’s part of the legal action the company takes here. But it’s also using “technical detection” to try to clamp down on cheat makers.
RICOCHET Anti-Cheat doesn't end when your match does.Cheat makers operate around the world. So do we. We’re taking the fight directly to cheat sellers.Last weekend during the Closed Beta, we went to Ohio to takedown Elocarry.That’s not an isolated case... pic.twitter.com/IP69qlGgDD
Activision said it’s “disrupted” more than 375 reseller operations, issued more than 80 cease-and-desist demands, and helped shut down 31 primary cheat vendors. “Cheat sellers often use marketing tactics and social posts to make their operations look stable, even when they are under significant pressure,” Activision said. “We’ve seen cheat developers use social platforms to explain months of downtime with excuses like ‘the flu,’ ‘surgery,’ or a ‘car accident’ rather than acknowledge their products were detected and no longer reliable. Those messages are part of the playbook they use to reassure customers while our systems continue disrupting their networks.”
Activision also pointed out that cheating is getting more expensive off the back of pressure it’s applying to the ecosystem. But still, some of the figures it’s released are eye-watering. It said cheaters could spend more than $1,000 a year just to cheat, when you consider some subscription cheats can cost upwards of $100 on the higher end, and spoofers add another recurring fee. DMA-related hardware and services drive the cost even more.
“Over the course of one year, some players spend hundreds of dollars — if not thousands — trying to maintain access to cheats, evasion tools, and replacement accounts,” Activision said. “Ultimately, cheating is a losing investment. Every time we identify and remove a bad actor, the money they spent cheating goes with them — all for a temporary ego boost.”
As always, the proof of the pudding is in the eating. Most accept Activision will never stamp cheating out of Call of Duty entirely, but the hope is that it will be less prevalent in Modern Warfare 4 than it has been in previous years.
Earlier this month, IGN interviewed David Andrews, Senior Director of Game Security for Call of Duty, to dispel some myths about Call of Duty cheating — and the work Activision does to prevent it.
Modern Warfare 4 launches October 22.

item.title: Tickets are now on sale online and at participating theatre box offices for the 20th Anniversary theatrical re-release of V for Vendetta, which will be in theaters nationwide on November 1 and 5, 2026. The news was accompanied by a new trailer that features a reimagining of Tchaikovsky’s 1812 Overture by Jonathan Snipes of the experimental hip-hop group clipping.
item.description:
Warner Bros. Motion Picture Group, Saga Arts, and Fathom Entertainment announced Friday that tickets are now on sale online and at participating box offices for the 20th Anniversary theatrical re-release of V for Vendetta, which will be in theaters nationwide on November 1 and 5, 2026.
The news was accompanied by a new trailer for the re-release, which can be viewed below. The trailer features an anniversary-inspired reimagining of Tchaikovsky’s 1812 Overture by Jonathan Snipes of the experimental hip-hop group clipping.
Based on the iconic DC Vertigo graphic novel written by Alan Moore and illustrated by David Lloyd, the 2004 film was directed by James McTeigue and produced by the Wachowskis.
The movie, like the graphic novel, is set in a futuristic totalitarian Britain where a young working class woman named Evey (Natalie Portman) encounters a masked freedom fighter known only as “V” (Hugo Weaving). Stephen Rea and John Hurt also star.
The 20th anniversary screenings will include Freedom Forever, an exclusive featurette where director McTeigue reflects on the making of the film and its relevance twenty years later.
“The award-winning V for Vendetta graphic novel led to one of the most provocative films in the early 2000s. Twenty years later, V for Vendetta still asks the questions that matter: about freedom, identity, and who gets to speak up. Fathom is thrilled to bring this great movie back to theatres, featuring an exclusive new conversation with director James McTeigue for a whole new generation of audiences,” said Shannah Miller, Vice President of Marketing at Fathom Entertainment in a statement.
V for Vendetta has found its way on many IGN lists in the years since it came out, including our picks for the 15 best R-rated superhero movies, the 25 best superhero movies, and the darkest superhero movies ever made.

item.title: Gen. Dan Caine, the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, says the United States military must be prepared to one day fight battles on the moon. Or real close to the moon, depending on how the term “cislunar” is read.
item.description:
We learned earlier this week that the US has deployed its first secretive space weapon in orbit above Earth. Now, the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff says the United States military must be prepared to one day fight battles on the moon. Or real close to the moon, depending on how the term “cislunar” is read.
As reported by Defense One, General Dan Caine made the following remarks in his recent keynote address at the Air, Space, and Cyber Conference.
“Our task, my friends, is to adapt right now, so the Joint Force is prepared to fight, endure, and win, in global contested environments, from the seabed to cislunar space,” Caine said, later adding that “today’s modern battlefield operates from the seabed to cislunar space.”
But as Defense One points out, the definition of cislunar is vague when it comes to US law. Is it the region of space just outside of the moon or does it include the surface of the moon itself? Depends on who you ask, it seems.
There are, however, existing international agreements meant to restrict human activity on the moon to be “exclusively for peaceful purposes.”
The US already agreed to the Outer Space Treaty of 1967 that bans the building of lunar military bases, as well as any weapons testing or military exercises on the moon. Countries that signed the treaty can only use military personnel on the moon for “scientific research or for any other peaceful purposes shall not be prohibited.”
Concerns about the possibility of a future conflict in space or on the moon stems from the ongoing rivalry between the US and China.
“The U.S. needs better capabilities in cislunar space to ensure China complies with that obligation and doesn’t militarize the moon,” Aaron Brynildson, a space law professor at the University of Mississippi, told Defense One. “There’s a real coverage gap by the U.S. that needs closing.”
Brynildson fears it might already be too late to clarify existing space law language in regards to military actions outside of our planet: “Ultimately, I think the first space conflict might be the time when most of these rules get written.”

item.title: A Marvel’s Wolverine player has discovered a glitch that allows for out of bounds exploration right up to the edges of the map.
item.description:
A Marvel’s Wolverine player has discovered a glitch that allows for out of bounds exploration right up to the edges of the map.
Warning! Spoilers for Marvel’s Wolverine follow…
A YouTuber called “Turned” published a video showing how Logan is able to climb up and over a seemingly innocuous building to go out of bounds in the mission, The One That Got Away. From there is a huge area to explore — much bigger than the linear play space would suggest — packed with all sorts of fun out of bounds gubbins, such as floating trees, ground that may or may not lead you under the map, and of course, glitchy collision. Turned makes their way to the boundaries of the map, where the ground squares off.
Youtuber Turned is demonstrating how there are glitches through which you can actually check the areas of map which were planned for the game.It seems like the game was much more ambitious at one point and scaled back to be a safer/smaller game. pic.twitter.com/I1DuAMb11a
Turned then published another video showing a similar out of bounds glitch in the Japan environment. By simply jumping over some trucks, Logan can leave the mission area and avoid triggering the automatic respawn.
There’s more fun glitchy stuff here, including cars that phase through walls. In the video, Turned follows the cars, which just keep driving straight forward until they despawn. What a sorry existence. The pedestrians don’t seem bothered though.
Things then get weirder — Turned explores buildings with no interior, views floating NPCs, and that old chestnut, the T-pose. The out of bounds areas for Japan are more detailed than the The One That Got Away mission, complete with eating areas and shops with interiors.
We’ve seen similar videos for countless video games over the years. In the last year or so, I’ve reported on out of bounds efforts in everything from Crimson Desert to The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered. But what’s remarkable here is the ease with which Turned is able to go out of bounds. It’s no surprise to see players discover these glitches when all you have to do is climb up a wall or jump over a vehicle. I suspect developer Insomniac will be keen to plug the gap sooner rather than later.
How do glitches like these make their way into a video game? TT Games developer Tim Spencer offered an explanation in a post on social media.
“FYI there's a 99% chance QA will have caught this, but someone in production will have dropped it to a priority 2 or lower, and during triage when they needed to ship: pushed it to a later patch (I don't want to think that they dropped it as WNF - ‘Will Not Fix’),” he said.
Earlier this week, Insomniac said it’s planning to “further refine the player experience” based on feedback. One aspect Insomniac may be looking at is Wolverine’s infamous “fart gas,” which has become the butt of online jokes in recent weeks. Some have called for Insomniac to add the ability to disable Logan’s scent trail entirely from the game amid complaints about handholding.

item.title: Xbox fans report being blocked from 100% completion in various games due to so-called "phantom achievements" — despite having collected the full 1000 Gamerscore.
item.description:
Xbox fans report being blocked from 100% completion in various games due to so-called "phantom achievements" — despite having collected the full 1,000 Gamerscore.
A bug is currently showing progress in some Xbox games capped below 100%, even when all visible achievements have been collected. For those who grind out achievements or who care about their count of games at 100% completion, this is an annoying glitch — especially as Xbox is believed to be working on an equivalent to PlayStation's Platinum trophy feature in future.
Thankfully, the cause of the issue appears to have already been tracked down, and Xbox is aware of the problem. Writing on X/Twitter, Xbox fan DarkIxion noted that the bugged games all seemed to be those with time-limited 0 Gamerscore challenges.
As a day one Xbox One purchaser, I remember the console's short-lived timed challenges, which provided extra achievements beyond each game's base list. Dead Rising 3, Titanfall, and Call of Duty: Ghosts had them, as did several non-gaming apps such as Netflix and YouTube.
Completing the requirements for these limited-time objectives would unlock exclusive bonus achievements — and while they provided 0 Gamerscore, they could also unlock extra game artwork or other in-game bonuses.
Alguns jogos que fiz 1000g no Xbox estão com uma conquista a mais, e não é a conquista de 0g. Vão acrescentar a "platina"? Verifiquem aí pic.twitter.com/hxEPeKc3LK
For those who missed out on a challenge, these 0G achievements did not appear in the game's main achievement list or count towards a game's 1,000 Gamerscore. But technically they were still attached to the game's data behind the scenes — something that this new bug is apparently surfacing.
"We're looking into why this changed," wrote Xbox engineering lead Eden Marie, responding to reports on Twitter/X. "Thanks for the report!"
Earlier this week, Microsoft insisted it was yet to "finalize" any changes to Xbox Game Pass, after a potential leak detailed plans to drop the inclusion of new titles from day one.
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: GTA 5 has suffered a new leak that suggests Rockstar Games had ambitious, city-sized DLC plans for the game.
item.description:
GTA 5 has suffered a new leak that suggests Rockstar Games had ambitious, city-sized DLC plans for the game.
Reports emerging online today indicate a near 200GB version of the GTA 5 source code initially leaked in 2023 has now been made public, and interested parties are analyzing it as we speak. The highlight here is what looks like a Liberty City DLC for GTA 5 that obviously never saw the light of day (GTA Online’s enormous success steered Rockstar away from story DLC towards multiplayer focused updates).
According to X / Twitter user TJGM, the Liberty City DLC found in the files has been extrapolated and visualized to show just how much bigger this version of the city is compared to the one found in GTA 4. “Here's a look at the expanded Liberty City layout,” they tweeted. “This outline of the map is drawn based on where shorelines are, the lines indicate zones that play shoreline audio.”
There is speculation online that this Liberty City DLC may have been held back for GTA 6, but there is no evidence to suggest that is Rockstar’s plan.
More has emerged from this leak: Agent Trevor DLC mission names; cut vehicles, cut dialogue, cut cutscenes, and more on GTA 5. There also appears to be very early GTA 6 work in the files.
On Agent Trevor, GTA fans have known for some time that Rockstar worked on a single-player DLC for GTA 5 that would have seen Trevor assume the role of a secret agent. In 2024, actor Steven Ogg said Rockstar originally planned to make a story expansion focused on his character, Trevor, with it thought to have fallen by the wayside as the developer focused on the cash cow that was GTA Online.
Ogg was joined by Michael actor Ned Luke and Franklin actor Shawn Fonteno in a Questions and Answers session with Streamily, and the trio shed light on what they claimed was scrapped downloadable content for GTA 5 that starred Trevor as a Federal Investigation Bureau agent.
"Originally they were gonna do continuing stories of Michael, Franklin, and Trevor," Luke said, and Ogg expanded on his version. "We also had that really cool s**t of — and I forget if it was DLC, I have no idea — but where Trevor was gonna be undercover, he works for the FEDs," Ogg said. "And we did shoot some of that stuff with James Bond Trevor. He's still kind of a f**k up but he's doing his best. And we shot some stuff and then it just disappeared and they never followed up on it."
Also in 2024, Joe Robino, who was a senior camera artist and virtual cinematographer working at Rockstar’s New York office from 2010 to 2016, spoke to the SanInPlay YouTube channel about why the GTA 5 story DLC was canceled.
“A lot of the team went to do Red Dead Redemption 2 right away and I took on this other project that was a standalone DLC for GTA that never came out and it was kick ass,” Robino revealed.
“That was my thing. I was one of the main editors, camera artists, and on-stage stuff. We split our teams into two. I stayed on GTA Online and then this DLC, which Steven Ogg [the actor who played Trevor Philips] was a very important part of.
“And then some of the team overlapped and went to RDR2 early on, and then we just kind of did this [flipped motion], because when that game got shelved, we spent so much money… a lot of that stuff though did end up making it I believe into later iterations of GTA Online, I think. So it’s not like they wasted it.
“It was really really good. But when GTA Online came out it was so much of a cash cow and people were loving it so much that it was hard to make an argument that a standalone DLC would outcompete that. I think looking back now you could probably do both. But that was a business decision they made. I was a little upset about that.
“That actually was a lot of the reason for me being a little sour at that time. Because I was like yo, WTF guys? This s**t’s awesome. Let’s keep going. Let’s finish this s**t.”
Fans have had snippets of information about GTA 5’s fabled story DLC over the years. GTA dataminers have also discovered a reference to Trevor with a jetpack, which suggests story mode DLC was repurposed into GTA Online, as Robino said. In 2018, Rockstar finally unveiled GTA Online's Doomsday Heist missions alongside the Thruster jetpack.
Last year, speaking on the Lex Fridman podcast, Rockstar Games co-founder and former lead writer Dan Houser addressed the DLC for the first time, insisting that if the developer had continued with it, it wouldn’t have been able to make 2018’s Red Dead Redemption 2.
“The internet knows we made a DLC… single-player DLC for GTA 5 that never came out,” Houser said.
“It was one when you played as Trevor, but he was a secret agent. It was cute. It never quite came together, and it was never finished. It was about half done when it got abandoned. But I think if that had come out, we probably wouldn’t have gotten to make Red Dead 2. So, there are always compromises.”
What approach will Rockstar take with GTA 6? Will it go back to story DLC, or focus on whatever new version of GTA Online it has up its sleeve? Some think Rockstar will eventually add multiple cities, including Liberty City, to GTA 6, alongside GTA Online 2 or whatever the multiplayer mode ends up being called. For now, though, it’s a case of what might have been for GTA 5.
Last week, as part of the ongoing employment tribunal to determine the fate of the 31 GTA 6 developers Rockstar fired last year, the company revealed the extreme lengths it goes to in order to prevent security breaches.
Rockstar has suffered a string of high-profile leaks over the years, most recently the 'CyberLeek' incident which saw GTA 6 gameplay hit the internet ahead of the game's Netflix special. Speaking at the tribunal, Rockstar said it's under intense scrutiny as the developer of GTA.
“Guarding the secrets of the unique gameplay and design are akin to Apple protecting the iPhone or Coke protecting its formula,” Rockstar said, adding that it adopts “the security posture of a Wall Street bank.”
In April 2025, Rockstar dismissed an employee in Lincoln, UK, who it alleged disclosed confidential information about GTA 6 to a third party who then published the information to social media. Rockstar dismissed an employee in the U.S. in November 2023 and another in India in November 2025 for two separate acts of information leaking.
Rockstar pointed out the frequency of coffee shop trips by employees and pizza deliveries to the Rockstar offices have been monitored by fans, and traffic volumes by its workplaces were allegedly tracked in a bid to get an inside track on the GTA 6 release date.
Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

item.title: There is a generation of gamers who know Turok well. For me, it is first and foremost an N64 game, a dinosaur-killing first-person shooter alternative to Rare’s all-conquering GoldenEye. But there is a generation of gamers who have never even heard of Turok before, let alone played it. So how does developer Saber get younger gamers interested in playing the upcoming Turok: Origins?
item.description:
There is a generation of gamers who know Turok well. For me, it is first and foremost an N64 game, a dinosaur-killing first-person shooter alternative to Rare’s all-conquering GoldenEye. But there is a generation of gamers who have never even heard of Turok before, let alone played it. So how does developer Saber get younger gamers interested in playing the upcoming Turok: Origins?
The answer, Saber development chief Tim Willits told me at gamescom 2026, is co-op. Playing with friends is massively important for younger gamers, he said, and so Saber has made sure to include it as a feature.
“It's been a balancing act to make sure that we had enough elements in it to make guys like you happy, like the Cerebral [Bore] gun, some throwbacks to the original Turok player, some other elements,” Willits said. "You can play first-person or third-person. So we want guys like you to be like, ‘Oh, this is cool.’ And then the dinosaur bosses are awesome.
“But we also want to make sure that we can get fans who have never played a Turok game. Like my kids, they're 22, they have never even heard of Turok. So we want to also build a game that looks amazing, plays great. You can play it by yourself or with one friend or two friends. We want to appeal to new players that have never played a Turok game as well.
“That's been our guiding principle with Turok. Add things that people like you would appreciate and like, but build a game that could be attractive to new players.”
You can see this theory in action across the video game industry. While single-player games remain enormously popular, hangout games have generated and continue to generate billions of dollars. Battle royales such as PUBG and Fortnite were built on the back of groups of friends chatting while playing. COVID lockdowns only accelerated the need for video games as social spaces, with Call of Duty battle royale Warzone an early beneficiary. Extraction shooters such as Escape from Tarkov and, more recently, Arc Raiders, were also fueled by friends who played together. A lot of the appeal of Helldivers 2 came from the shenanigans you could get up to with your friends.
Then there’s the rise of ‘friendslop’ games, which are massive across Steam (Roblox clones are incredibly popular, too). And we have a perfect example of this appeal only recently: Bulkhead’s hit Steam game Wardogs is a shooter that revolves around playing with friends. “I truly believe it is not about the mode, it’s about letting players run wild,” Bulkhead boss Joe Brammer recently tweeted. “The more you constrain players the less fun it is, FPS games are social experiences and Wardogs is closer to Mecca Chameleon than COD.”
Enter Turok: Origins, which shouldn’t be compared to something like Wardogs or a battle royale, of course, but it does let teams of three players join up to shoot dinosaurs in the face. Think Space Marine 2 but instead of fighting Tyranids, you’re fighting dinosaurs with lasers.
“It looks amazing,” Willits continued. “The big giant boss fights — I'm not even sure if this is a term — do you know the boss run games? It has that kind of feel to it. And wait till you see some of our cool bosses! And then playing with the friends, it's really important to young gamers now. Like you and I are like, we play by ourselves. We're old. So you can play either way, but it's really important to a huge audience to at least have the option to play with someone else.
“Because young people use video games as a social connection more so than you and I did, because we grew up in different times. And so it looks great, play is fun. The Echoes [you collect Echoes to unlock Turok powers] are amazing. The boss runs are sweet and you can play with your friends. So I feel it has those elements that will attract new people.”
Turok: Origins is due out spring 2027 on PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and S, and Nintendo Switch 2. Check out our Turok: Origins hands-on preview for more.

item.title: Paul Bettany has claimed he still doesn't know if Elizabeth Olsen's Scarlet Witch will return in Vision Quest, but fans have hope.
item.description:
Paul Bettany has claimed he still doesn't know if Elizabeth Olsen's Scarlet Witch will return in VisionQuest.
The promising-looking Disney+ show is set to conclude the trilogy of series that began with WandaVision, and fan hopes are high that some kind of cameo from Wanda Maximoff will take place.
Audiences last saw Wanda during the finale of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness, as she brought down Mount Wundagore and was seemingly buried underneath a mountain of stone. But... we didn't see a body, and all comic book fans should know what that means!
Asked whether his on-screen partner would finally return in VisionQuest, Bettany told Entertainment Today that the answer to this was a secret that even he didn't know the answer to, sparking fan speculation that an appearance by Olsen may have been filmed.
"That is, at this point, a matter of secrecy," Bettany claimed. "And it's secret even to me. There are also other surprises to come, and other big reveals. It's very exciting, I think, the story is really compelling and interesting."
While VisionQuest is not directly about Wanda, fans still want to see Scarlet Witch return in some form. An appearance would help round out the WandaVision trilogy that began by focusing on her relationship with the re-animated synthezoid and continued by revealing that the couple's imaginary kids were now real. (It's complicated.)
Agatha All Along featured Heartstopper star Joe Locke as Billy Maximoff, while VisionQuest is set to introduce Ruaridh Mollica as Tommy Maximoff. Surely Marvel is building to a full family reunion, with Wanda included?
More pressing, though, is the expectation that Wanda will join the vast group of fan-favorite Marvel characters to appear in the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday and next year's Avengers: Secret Wars. Could a cameo for VisionQuest have been filmed recently? Avengers: Doomsday reshoots did recently take place — so perhaps Bettany really doesn't know yet if something has been added in post-production. Or, of course, he absolutely does know if Wanda is in the show (or not) and is simply keeping the truth hidden.
"I suspect the post credit scene will be Wanda alive and working for Doom," one fan speculated. "I think it’ll be from the recent Doomsday reshoots we know Elizabeth Olsen attended." (This references recent, unverified internet speculation prompted by a potential sighting of Olsen flying into the U.K. around the time Doomsday reshoots took place.)
"Especially since this show has repeatedly been referred to as the third in the Wanda-Vision family trilogy," a second fan replied. "If this is the end of a trilogy that began with her alone and manifesting a family which is then broken, scattered and reborn, it makes narrative sense for them to come together again at the close."
"Rule #1 no body, no death," said a third.
VisionQuest begins streaming on October 18 via Disney+, so there's not long until we find out.

item.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker is indeed getting a new game plus mode in the future, according to the game's director.
item.description:
The Blood of Dawnwalker is indeed getting a new game plus mode in the future, according to the game's director.
The Blood of Dawnwalker is one of the biggest games of September, and although it boasts a pretty lengthy story, fans are already looking for reasons to replay it. Director Konrad Tomaszkiewicz confirmed on a stream (via GamesRadar) that the game is getting a new game plus mode, but neglected to share any further details. We're not sure when it will be released or what features it may include... but rest assured, it's coming!
The Blood of Dawnwalker has a unique structure that may lend itself well to new game plus. The player has 30 in-game days to essentially complete the main goal of the story, which is to save the protagonist's family. Time passes when you complete quests, so you have to be somewhat selective about what adventures you want to go on or risk wasting your limited days.
Similarly, upgrading skills can also advance time, meaning you can't max out your character. However, if the game had new game plus, it might encourage players to replay the game over and over again until they've maxed out their character or completed every quest. It's almost like a Groundhog Day situation, in theory.
Of course, this is only speculative. We have no idea how it will look, but the entire purpose of new game plus is to add replay value by allowing players to carry over gear, skills, and other buffs to new playthroughs of the game. Hopefully we won't have to wait too long to find out, but if there's anything we've learned about developer Rebel Wolves so far, it's that it won't dilly-dally.
The developer is already hiring for its next game, which is expected to be a sequel to The Blood of Dawnwalker, though potentially in a new setting and era. The studio foresees this as a franchise that spans centuries, so we should get some unique stories in future installments.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: In the wake of fierce online backlash, Professor Layton developer Level-5 has released a new statement apologizing for the mistrust caused by generative AI use in its recent showcase for upcoming titles, insisting some examples spotted by fans were simply human error.
item.description:
In the wake of fierce online backlash, Professor Layton developer Level-5 has released a new statement apologizing for the mistrust caused by generative AI use in its recent showcase for upcoming titles, insisting some examples spotted by fans were simply human error.
Not only that, but the studio has insisted that some mistakes flagged as AI errors by eagle-eyed commenters on social media were actually human mistakes. The Japanese studio has now vowed to clean up these offending portions.
For those who missed it, Level-5 released its “VISION 2026 II: Dreams” presentation on YouTube on September 10. Narrated by a cartoon version of CEO Akihiro Hino, the showcase walked viewers through the studio’s upcoming releases, including Yokai Watch 2: Haunted Domain, Decapolice, and a first look at Professor Layton and the New World of Steam.
However, shortly after the video dropped, social media was flooded with comments and reaction videos. Commenters scrutinized backgrounds and art, noting inconsistencies and elements suggestive of generative AI use, with many slamming Level-5 for perceived “AI slop.” Comparisons between the September 9 Nintendo Direct Yokai Watch 2 trailer and the VISION 2026 trailer for the same game released just a day later also had fans pointing out AI-like errors. The Nintendo Direct trailer for Professor Layton and the Curious Village (a Switch remake of the Nintendo DS original), also had internet sleuths finding elements that appeared to be AI upscales of original backgrounds.
Oh no Level-5 is DEFINATELY using Gen AI to "update" Professor Layton. Especially when you compare the original backgrounds to the new. So many weird details and inconsistencies were added. https://t.co/AjVNfgetkk pic.twitter.com/0tRQ9vKn03
This backlash prompted CEO Hino to make a statement on X, admitting that the developer had experimented with using AI processing techniques for the VISION 2026 II showcase out of a “desire to make the presentation flashy." After apologizing for the offense that this caused, Hino insisted that key elements of Level-5's games (such as story, character designs and settings) were created by people and that AI tools were used to speed up the process of digitizing artists’ creations. “Please be reassured that there is no simplistic, AI-generated data in our released games,” Hino commented, before noting that the company’s use of AI tools to make processes more efficient was giving its developers more time to be creative, and that they are currently in a trail-and-error process of shortening the 5-year development cycle for major titles down to two years.
Hino’s statement went down like a lead balloon, however. The CEO’s comments about “using AI in various ways” to enhance the visual appearance of the showcase drew particular ire, with many Japanese users seeing this as a lazy ‘style over substance’ approach. “Isn’t the point of a trailer to express creativity, not flashiness?” one person said.
Many commenters in both Japanese and English also pointed out the ethical issues with how generative AI has been trained on copyrighted works of artists, and how Level-5’s attitude towards gen AI creates distrust among fans. “I think human spirit is more important than the speed of game releases, so wouldn’t it be better to not use AI, even if it takes five years? Even if just one asset is AI-generated, people will never stop worrying about whether a song, image or line of dialogue is AI or human-made. Isn’t maintaining trust the most important thing?” another commenter responded in Japanese. As a side note, Level-5’s concept image for its TGS booth also got flagged as a suspected AI image, prompting further angry comments.
In its latest statement issued on September 17, Level-5 said: “We deeply apologize for the distrust in our production process that our inexperienced use of AI and simple human errors have caused. Please note that AI has not been used directly in the contents of the games themselves. Moving forward, we will pay even greater attention to the accuracy and quality of the work we produce.”
Level-5 also said that it will clean up “errors caused by AI use, as well as human mistakes that look like AI errors,” and upload corrected versions of the trailers to coincide with Tokyo Game Show, which opens to the public this weekend. At the time of writing, Level-5 has uploaded TGS versions of trailers for Decapolice and Holy Horror Mansion to its official YouTube channel.
In its September 17 statement, Level-5 published a side-by-side of Yokai Watch 2’s promotional illustration before and after mistakes had been edited out. Addressing comments made by users regarding the telephone lines looking “unnatural,” the company stated that its artist had used a real photo of telephone lines they had taken themselves as a reference, and intentionally simplified the lines to fit the background, which resulted in this “being misconstrued as AI.” “These telephone lines were actually hand-drawn by our in-house designer, however, to prevent any further misunderstandings, we have corrected them so that they look more natural,” Level-5 said.
But what about other details flagged by commenters as possible signs of gen AI usage? Level-5 said that, “Similarly, other issues that people pointed out, such as with the vending machine and guttering, were also the result of human error in omitting these details. The brake levers on the bicycle were not drawn in past Yokai Watch 2 games. However, we feel they should have been drawn for this latest game, considering the higher level of detail.”
⁉️ Dans le nouveau trailer de Yo-kai Watch 2 : Haunted Domain, Nathan a… changé de visage ?! 😭#YOKAIWATCHHier (gauche) / Aujourd’hui (droite) pic.twitter.com/Vr3rzwNPA7
Many commenters also picked up on how Kenta/Nathan’s face looks different in the Level-5’s VISION 2026 II showcase and the Nintendo Direct that was released on the previous day. In response, Level-5 said, “We did not make any alterations or corrections using AI.” It said it was unable to correct Nathan’s low-poly appearance in time for Nintendo Direct’s submission deadline but had updated the model by the time of its own showcase, which explains why Nathan looks different in trailers that were made public just one day apart. Level-5 also stated that “no AI was used in Professor Layton and the New World of Steam,” however it did not comment on whether or not AI was used for the Curious Village remake.
Level-5 wrapped up its statement by apologizing again for the distrust caused by its “inexperienced use of AI and human error," promising to take more care in the future to avoid such mistakes. “From now on, we will limit our AI usage to enhancing efficiency, and will avoid directly using it in videos released directly to our fans.”
This statement also did not go down well. “I don’t think they understand WHY using AI is bad. We weren’t mad at the little errors that AI produced, we just used those errors to determine if it was AI or not, because using AI at all is bad. Now they are going to continue using AI but they are going to hide it better,” one commenter responded.
It's not about reducing the use of AI, but about eliminating it entirely. pic.twitter.com/ziJuMrxBsm
Many Japanese comments also criticized the Level-5 statement for blaming human error. “You promised not to use gen AI going forward, but aren’t you just shifting the blame onto the staff?” replied one commenter. “I think the main reason for all this criticism is President Hino’s stance of repeatedly promoting generative AI usage without confronting its fundamental issues (such as unauthorized use of data and environmental pollution).”
Level-5 has been experimenting with gen AI tools to speed up game development and improve efficiency for at least the last three years. Back in December 2023, the studio released an extensive presentation on its use of AI tools to a Japanese government study group (source: Automaton/ITMedia). In short, it has been using Stable Diffusion to generate layout ideas for promotions, and to create 3D versions of the original 2D models from older games, like its Yokai Watch series. However, the company pointed out then that these generative AI outputs were just used as guidelines for its human artists, who produced the final output. In the same presentation, it described combining parts of AI-generated images with creations by its artists to make the in-game backgrounds (including stadium crowds and buildings) for soccer RPG Inazuma Eleven: Victory Road.
However, it remains to be seen how much the studio’s attitude towards AI usage costs it in terms of players’ trust in the company.
